questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Hand signals help riders communicate when riding in groups. This signal means "follow me."

questions.question: Where should you place a load?

options.text: On one side of the motorcycle

questions.explanation: Keep loads low and secure them in saddlebags. Placing loads high on the back raises the motorcycle's center of gravity and makes it harder to balance. Always spread weight evenly on both sides of the motorcycle.

questions.question: What does an integrated braking system do?

options.text: Applies partial rear braking when the front brake is applied.
Applies partial front braking when the rear brake is applied.
Applies equal braking to both front and rear brakes when either is used.
Learns and remembers how hard the rider brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Applies partial front braking when the rear brake is applied.
questions.explanation: An integrated braking system applies some front braking whenever you use the rear brake. Check your owner's manual to learn more about your motorcycle's braking system.

questions.question: What is the minimum following distance you should maintain?
questions.explanation: Keep at least two seconds between you and the vehicle ahead. In bad weather or poor conditions, increase this to at least three seconds.

questions.question: How should you brake during normal stops?

options.text: Use both the front and rear brakes.
Switch between the front and rear brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both the front and rear brakes.
questions.explanation: Always use both brakes when you slow down or stop, even for normal stops.

questions.question: How can you keep other vehicles from sharing your lane?

options.text: Ride in the middle of your lane.
Ride in the left portion of your lane.
Ride in the right portion of your lane.
Swerve side to side in your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the middle of your lane.
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of your lane to discourage car drivers from trying to share it with you.

questions.question: What percentage of motorcycle and car crashes happen because the driver fails to yield right-of-way?
questions.explanation: More than half of all motorcycle and car crashes happen because the driver fails to yield right-of-way to the motorcycle.

questions.question: How should you stop behind a vehicle?

options.text: Stop far back, then slowly move closer.
Stay about four car lengths behind.

questions.explanation: Keep a good distance behind the vehicle in front of you. The vehicle could back up without warning, or you may need to move quickly if another vehicle approaches from behind.

questions.question: How should you brake on a slippery surface?

options.text: Do not use brakes; downshift instead.

questions.explanation: On slippery surfaces, slow down and avoid sudden movements. Use both brakes gently if you need to stop.

questions.question: Should you wear a leather jacket when it is warm outside?

options.text: No, it will make you too hot.
Yes, but take breaks to remove it and cool off.
Yes, riding jackets are made to keep riders cool in warm weather.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, riding jackets are made to keep riders cool in warm weather.
questions.explanation: Riding jackets help prevent dehydration and provide protection in all weather. Modern jackets are designed to keep riders cool, even when it is warm outside.

questions.question: When riding, you should:

options.text: Turn your head and shoulders to look through turns.
Keep your knees away from the gas tank.
Turn just your head and eyes to look through turns.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn just your head and eyes to look through turns.
questions.explanation: When turning, look ahead to where you want to go. Turn only your head, not your shoulders. Keep your eyes level with the horizon.

questions.question: How often should you check a motorcycle's hydraulic fluid at minimum?
questions.explanation: Check your hydraulic fluid and coolants at least once a week as part of your regular motorcycle maintenance.

questions.question: Which type of sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They alert you to upcoming road conditions.

questions.question: Your lane position should do all of the following, except:

options.text: Increase your ability to see and be seen.
Prevent access to an escape route.

questions.correctAnswerText: Prevent access to an escape route.
questions.explanation: Good lane positioning helps you see and be seen, avoid blind spots and hazards, and discourages sharing your lane. It should always keep an escape route available in case of danger.

questions.question: Under normal conditions, what is the minimum following distance you should maintain?
questions.explanation: Keep at least four seconds of distance behind the vehicle ahead under normal conditions. Increase this distance when conditions are poor.

questions.question: When preparing to pass another rider on the left, you should:

options.text: Get into the right part of the lane so you can be seen in their side mirror.
Get into the left part of the lane to increase your line of sight.
Stay in the center part of the lane so you can be seen in their rearview mirror.
Weave in your lane to draw attention to yourself.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get into the left part of the lane to increase your line of sight.
questions.explanation: Move to the left part of your lane before passing. This improves your view ahead and makes you more visible. Always check mirrors and look over your shoulder before changing lanes.

questions.question: Normally, what is the recommended following distance?
questions.explanation: Under normal conditions, keep at least two seconds of distance from the vehicle ahead. Increase this distance if conditions are not ideal.

questions.question: When you park a motorcycle next to a curb, how should it be positioned?

options.text: Parked at a 90-degree angle with the rear wheel touching the curb.
Parked at a 45-degree angle with the front tire touching the curb.
Parked like a car, with the front and rear wheels the same distance from the curb.
Parked at the left edge of the parking space so approaching drivers can more easily see the motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Parked at a 90-degree angle with the rear wheel touching the curb.
questions.explanation: Park at a 90-degree angle to the curb with your rear wheel touching it.

questions.question: When looking through a turn, you should:

options.text: Turn both your head and your shoulders to get a better look.
Turn just your head, not your shoulders.
Only move your eyes, not your head.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn just your head, not your shoulders.
questions.explanation: Look ahead through the turn to where you want to go. Turn only your head, not your shoulders. Keep your eyes level with the horizon.

questions.question: Which of these signs may be rectangular?
questions.explanation: Speed limit signs are rectangular with white background and black lettering. They tell you the rules you must follow on that road.

questions.question: When going through a curve, what should you do?

options.text: Stay in the same part of your lane the whole time.
Stay in the left part of your lane the whole time.
Stay in the right part of your lane the whole time.
Remember that the best path may not follow the road's curve.

questions.correctAnswerText: Remember that the best path may not follow the road's curve.
questions.explanation: Road and traffic conditions change. Be ready to move your lane position when needed. The best path through a curve may not match the road's curve exactly.

questions.question: Studies show most riders in crashes:

options.text: Don't brake the front tire enough and brake the rear tire too much.
Brake the front tire too much and don't brake the rear tire enough.

questions.correctAnswerText: Don't brake the front tire enough and brake the rear tire too much.
questions.explanation: Most riders in crashes don't brake the front tire enough and brake the rear tire too much.

questions.question: When entering a turn, what should a rider do?

options.text: Move your shoulders to match the turn's angle.

questions.explanation: Before entering a turn, slow down by releasing the throttle and using the brakes if needed.

questions.question: Lane sharing is:

options.text: Allowed in heavy traffic to use space better.
Allowed if there is enough space for both vehicles.

questions.explanation: Motorcycles need a full lane width to be safe. Lane sharing is not allowed.

questions.question: What is a linked braking system?

options.text: The front and rear brakes work together. When you use either brake, both brakes engage.
The front brake connects to the gear shifter. The brake engages when you downshift.
The rear brake connects to a foot control.
The rear brake connects to a switch on the handlebar.

questions.correctAnswerText: The front and rear brakes work together. When you use either brake, both brakes engage.
questions.explanation: A linked braking system connects the front and rear brakes. When you use either brake lever, both brakes get pressure. Check your owner's manual for details about your motorcycle's braking system.
